content.intro: This lesson focuses on github authentication methods. Use the example to predict the workflow result, then verify the behavior in a safe test repository or by static review.
content.why_it_matters: GitHub Authentication Methods matters because it affects correctness, security, maintainability, or operating cost. content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Choose between `GITHUB_TOKEN`, a fine-grained personal access token, and a GitHub App token based on required access, lifetime, repository scope, and rotation. Security starts with least privilege and trust boundaries: scope tokens, store credentials as secrets, isolate untrusted contributions, and prefer short-lived federated credentials when available. The most useful check is one that produces observable evidence and fails clearly when its stated requirement is not met.

items.title: GITHUB_TOKEN
items.text: Declare only the token scopes the job requires. A read-only job should not receive write access; verify permissions at workflow and job scope and review organization policy.

items.title: Credential storage
items.text: Store credentials in the appropriate protected secret store, pass them only to the step that needs them, and never print or save them in logs, summaries, artifacts, or caches.

items.title: Choosing authentication for automation
items.text: For choosing authentication for automation, state the expected input and result, identify the relevant workflow field or operational decision, and verify it with a controlled check plus run logs. Document the failure condition rather than relying on the YAML file merely parsing.

content_blocks.code:
name: Read-only validation
on: workflow_dispatch
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  inspect:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: echo "Choose authentication by scope, lifetime, and required repositories"
content_blocks.expected_output: This workflow itself needs only read access. Use a GitHub App or fine-grained token only when the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN cannot meet the documented access requirements.

items.title: Syntax and scope
items.text: Check YAML indentation and confirm whether the setting belongs at workflow, job, or step level.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain github authentication methods, read the example, and identify a way to validate it. The wider system goal remains: Constrain credentials and token permissions, and prefer scoped, short-lived authentication where supported.

troubleshooting: If a workflow never starts, verify the workflow is under `.github/workflows/`, the event and filters match, and repository/organization Actions policy allows it.
If a step fails, inspect the first failed step, exit code, stderr, installed tool versions, permissions, and runner/network state before retrying.
If a job is skipped or data is missing, inspect `if`, `needs`, outputs, artifact names/paths, and cache keys; jobs do not automatically share filesystems.
common_mistakes: Assuming YAML parsing proves the workflow runs correctly or matches the intended trigger.
Granting broad token permissions, printing environment values, or exposing a secret to untrusted code.
Using a placeholder command as evidence of a real build, test, deployment, or security scan.
